entries.label: scene
entries.text: (Resumption of Debate on Motion on Establishment of Impeachment Committee)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: This means we must finish our business by 6.30 p.m. I, therefore, call upon the Mover to reply.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Kipchumba Murkomen
entries.text: On a point of order, Mr. Speaker, Sir.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Order, Members! Just a minute. Sen. Kibiru, you will have to finish because we must conclude this by 6.30 p.m. He was on the Floor.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Charles Reubenson Kibiru
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, as I conclude, the people of Kirinyaga County are watching and it is unfortunate that the die is cast. I can tell the people of Kirinyaga that going the Committee way means that the verdict is known. I seriously oppose the Motion.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: I call upon the Mover to reply.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Farhiya Ali Haji
entries.text: I am the Mover, and I donate my time to the Senate Majority Leader and the Senate Minority Leader.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Kipchumba Murkomen
entries.text: Point of Order! Point of Order!

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Order! Order, Sen. Murkomen, Order!

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Kipchumba Murkomen
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I am on a point of order, which is important. I know that you have called the Mover to reply. We cannot challenge the decision of the Speaker because we have to respect the operation of the House. There is a huge constituency that has been disenfranchised in this House; the ones that were opposed to the question of forming the Committee. The people of Kirinyaga are watching us and they know that there were issues we wanted to say related to them.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (Loud consultations)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Kipchumba Murkomen
entries.text: I am asking for your indulgence. Out of the 18 minutes remaining, you should have given us eight minutes to make something.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (Loud consultations)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Order! We will not conclude this matter since we have to vote the Roll Call way. We will go beyond time. We have had time to express ourselves. Let me call the Senate Minority Leader to conclude.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: James Orengo
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, if you look at the Constitution of Kenya in the area that deals with Parliament, Committees are provided for as an integral part of Parliament. The same powers given to Parliament in Plenary are given to Committees. Committees can summon witnesses.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Kipchumba Murkomen
entries.text: Point of Order! Mr. Speaker, Sir, I thought you had called the Mover to reply?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Order, Sen. Murkomen! The Mover had donated some few minutes to the Senate Majority Leader and the Senate Minority Leader. Proceed, Sen. Orengo.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Kipchumba Murkomen
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, is it not the same issue that I said you are disenfranchising us?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Order, Sen. Murkomen! Proceed, Sen. Orengo.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: James Orengo
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, having said that, this Senate should never be in a position where there is dictation on how we handle our business. This is a very important institution. In fact, if you go by why in the federalist papers they say the Senate is an important institution, you will know that we are here because the Standing Orders and the Constitution give us powers to make the decisions we are making. I would like to say this as I finish. Salome the daughter of Herod danced so well for Herod. When Herod asked her want she wanted, she asked for the head of John the Baptist. Today, some people have danced so well. They are not looking for justice, but for somebody's head. That head is not for Salome, but for somebody. Gov. Waiguru's head is being asked for, not by the County Assembly; I can tell you that and I have the evidence. The people looking for Waiguru's head is not the County Assembly.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Kipchumba Murkomen
entries.text: On a point of order! On a point of order, Mr. Speaker, Sir.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Order!

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Kipchumba Murkomen
entries.text: On a point of order!

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (Loud consultations)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Order, Members!

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: An hon. Senator
entries.text: We are not looking for the head of the governor.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (Sen. Kwamboka stood in her place)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Sen. Kwamboka, sit down.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (Sen. Kwamboka resumed her seat)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: We have to conclude. What is it, Sen. Kihika?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Susan Wakarura Kihika
entries.text: On a point of order, Mr. Speaker, Sir. Is it in order for Sen. Orengo, who is the Senate Minority Leader, to impute improper motive in this House, when we know very clearly that the Impeachment Motion was brought by the County Assembly of Kirinyaga? Why should he continue lecturing us here on nonsense, if I may say? It is inappropriate.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Kipchumba Murkomen
entries.text: On a point of order! On a point of order, Mr. Speaker, Sir!

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Order!

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Kipchumba Murkomen
entries.text: You said that you would give me a chance.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Order! Can you sit down?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Kipchumba Murkomen
entries.text: On a point of order, Mr. Speaker, Sir.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Just a minute. Sen. Kihika was on the Floor and you know the Standing Orders. You cannot be on the Floor at the same time. Hon. Senators, the whole world is watching us. Let us conduct ourselves with decorum. We do not have time.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Kipchumba Murkomen
entries.text: On a point of order, Mr. Speaker, Sir!

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Senate Minority Leader, can you contribute?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Kipchumba Murkomen
entries.text: On a point of order, Mr. Speaker, Sir. We have been accused---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Order! We must conclude.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Kipchumba Murkomen
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, you said that you would give me a chance.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Sen. Murkomen, I have given you a lot of time.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Kipchumba Murkomen
entries.text: On a point of order, Mr. Speaker, Sir.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Sen. Orengo, can you conclude?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Kipchumba Murkomen
entries.text: We cannot allow that to go on record.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: I will make a ruling.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Kipchumba Murkomen
entries.text: On a point of order, Mr. Speaker, Sir.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: James Orengo
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, with those remarks, I support. The stone has heard me.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Kipchumba Murkomen
entries.text: On a point of order, Mr. Speaker, Sir!

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: I will allow Sen. (Dr.) Langat to say something. We do not have time.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Christopher Andrew Langat
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, it is wrong for Senior Counsel, Sen. Orengo, to cast aspersions on Members of this House as a group of people who are after the head of somebody. We never initiated this Motion; it was initiated by Kirinyaga County Assembly. He should withdraw that.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Kipchumba Murkomen
entries.text: On a point of order, Mr. Speaker, Sir!

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Order, Members! Let us proceed. Senate Majority Leader.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Kipchumba Murkomen
entries.text: On a point of order, Mr. Speaker, Sir.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Order, Members!

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Aaron Kipkirui Cheruiyot
entries.text: On a point of order, Mr. Speaker, Sir.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Order, Members. Proceed, Senate Majority Leader.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Kipchumba Murkomen
entries.text: On a point of order, Mr. Speaker, Sir.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Aaron Kipkirui Cheruiyot
entries.text: On a point of order, Mr. Speaker, Sir. Just one.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Order, Members.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Kipchumba Murkomen
entries.text: I am standing on a point of order, Mr. Speaker, Sir.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Aaron Kipkirui Cheruiyot
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, please, one.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Samuel Poghisio
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, in supporting this Motion---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Kipchumba Murkomen
entries.text: We are on a point of order, Mr. Speaker, Sir.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Samuel Poghisio
entries.text: I appeal---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Order! Order!

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Susan Wakarura Kihika
entries.text: On a point of order, Mr. Speaker, Sir.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Aaron Kipkirui Cheruiyot
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, on a health issue. There is a health issue.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Order! Order!

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Kipchumba Murkomen
entries.text: There is a record that must be corrected.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Moses Otieno Kajwang'
entries.text: You cannot force the Speaker to allow you to raise a point of order.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Kipchumba Murkomen
entries.text: There is a record that must be corrected.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: I am giving you one minute, Sen. Murkomen.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Kipchumba Murkomen
entries.text: Thank you, Mr. Speaker, Sir. The people of Kirinyaga have all along this week suspected that there is a decision already made elsewhere to form a Committee to save Gov. Waiguru.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Order! Order, Sen. Murkomen, Order!

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Kipchumba Murkomen
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, and then Sen. Orengo goes public to confirm- -- He goes on record to confirm that a decision has already been made---.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Order, Senator!

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Kipchumba Murkomen
entries.text: If this Committee is going to sanitize Gov. Waiguru, they should tell us the truth.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Order! Order, Sen. Murkomen!

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Kipchumba Murkomen
entries.text: I want to tell the people of Kirinyaga that a decision has already been made and this Committee is a sanitizing committee---

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (Loud Consultations)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Order, Sen. Murkomen!

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Kipchumba Murkomen
entries.text: This is a sanitizing Committee.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (Loud Consultations)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text:
Order! Order, Sen. Murkomen! An hon. Senator:

Toa yeye nje

. Chase him out!

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Samuel Poghisio
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, Standing Order No.116 will bear you out on people who cause these kinds of problems. The verdict that is coming out of here is from the Senate. It shall be owned by the Senate because Committees are owned by the Senate. I support and ask that we move in this direction, so that we can conclude and vote. We can then determine the direction and that is going to be owned by the Senate. Thank you.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Order, Members. The Mover had donated time. I will now put the question.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Kipchumba Murkomen
entries.text: On a point of order, Mr. Speaker, Sir. Before putting the question, the Standing Order---.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Order, Members!

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Kipchumba Murkomen
entries.text: There is a constitutional question---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Order, Sen. Murkomen.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Kipchumba Murkomen
entries.text: There is a constitutional question; you have to determine whether or not it concerns counties.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Order, Members!

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: An. hon. Senator
entries.text: You cannot just continue with a procedure like that.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Order, Members!

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Kipchumba Murkomen
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, there is a constitutional procedure that you are jumping, and we must say it.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Wait! Order, Members! I know. When we voted here, my last ruling was that it was not a matter affecting counties.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Kipchumba Murkomen
entries.text: But you have not ruled today.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Wait! Order, Sen. Murkomen! Even in Gov. Waititu case, all Members voted. So, I am saying it is not a matter concerning counties.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Kipchumba Murkomen
entries.text: You should say that. That was the point I was trying to tell you.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: As I said, we will use the Roll Call vote. The voice vote cannot work because of the extended Chamber. We are going to do exactly as we did in the other voting. The Deputy Speaker and a Clerk will now go and get the votes there as we start ours here under the guidance of the Deputy Clerk. The Division Bell will be rung for one minute as the Deputy Speaker goes to the extended Chamber.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (The Division Bell was rung)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Can we start because time is not on our side? Hon. Senators, take your seats. The Majority Whip, take your seat. You are the one who is supposed to be organizing your people. I direct that the Bar be drawn and the doors locked.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (The Bar was drawn and the doors closed)

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (The Senators proceeded to vote by Roll Call)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: I direct that the doors be opened.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (The doors were opened)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: I am using my powers under Standing Order No.31 (2), which states: "Unless for the convenience of the Senate, the Speaker or the Chairperson (as the case may be) in this case being the Speaker, directs earlier or later interruption of business at 6.30 pm., the Speaker or the Chairperson shall interrupt the business then under consideration and if the Senate is in Committee, the Chairperson shall leave the Chair and report progress and ask for leave to sit again." I am just waiting for the report. I wanted to use my powers under that section. Order, Members! Kindly, take your seats!

entries.text:
DIVISION
ROLL CALLVOTING

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (Question, that the Senate establishes a Special Committee to investigate the proposed removal from office by impeachment of the Governor of Kirinyaga County, put and the Senate proceeded to vote)
